checks: Source db95f50a50308952 §5 (7) supplies the hull conclusion, and dbf59e16706aadc7 §7 (12)–(14) gives the underlying one-base comparison. The frozen theorem assumes the numerical gap and does not invoke the selected-minimum proof of that gap.

The closed base trace ℓ(z)≥ℓ(p) contains p and carries at least b(p) in raw original fiber volume. A constant trace uses the total mass, including base rank zero. If ℓ(p)≥0 this trace is fully captured by A≥0 and contradicts Q<b(p).

On that trace any missed point has 0≤A/c<−ℓ(p)/t. Since e is a unit covector this is a slab of exactly the relevant physical width. Fubini gives total missed volume at most A_sec times that width and at least b(p)−Q. The d=1 section bound uses counting measure.

Affinity extends the inequality to unsampled real bases in the convex hull. The resulting strict cutoff makes the margin negative for the same original closed cap. For a rank-zero fiber [0,3], A=2x and margin 3x−3, the bound is sharp with Q=2, b=3, g_0=1 and A_sec=1, and the cutoff endpoint is indeed captured.
